successors.note: 91 BC: 'After Rome refused them citizenship, the Samnites rebelled' (Samnites page), the Samnite group of the Italian confederation of the Social War (Cliopatria's Italian City-States, -91..-88); granted citizenship afterwards, punished by Sulla after the Colline Gate (82).

capitals.name: Bovianum (Bojano), the Pentri's capital
capitals.note: 'Bovianum is the capital of the Pentri'; the confederation had no capital of its own. Bovianum fell to Rome in 305/304 (ledger /8) yet stays the only Samnite centre a page names; confidence 1 after 304.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Samnite row; the page has no infobox area. Samnium by the provinces of Campobasso, Isernia, Benevento and Avellino (about 8,100 km2 by the gazetteer), 'a region located in the modern inland Abruzzo, Molise, and Campania'; four tribes, no central capital. Soft edges.

keyframe_review.note: From about 424 the Samnites hold Campania (Capua 'captured by the Samnites' c. 424; the Samnites page: the region, Pompeii, Herculaneum, Cumae, not Naples) apart from Caserta, which is Capua's own state until 343 (capua dossier). The First Samnite War (343-341) is a contest inside the shape.

region.text: Samnium: the Pentri (Bovianum), Caraceni, Caudini and Hirpini

ledger.note: c. 500 BC: the Samnite confederation. 'An Oscan-speaking Italic people who inhabited Samnium, a region in the modern inland Abruzzo, Molise, and Campania', who 'formed a confederation consisting of four tribes' (Hirpini, Caudini, Caraceni, Pentri; 'Bovianum is the capital of the Pentri'). No page dates the confederation; 500 is a placeholder before the first dated act, the conquest of Campania in the 5th century.

region.text: the Campanian plain of Capua, Pompeii and Herculaneum, Cumae

ledger.note: 424 BC: Campania. 'In about 424 BC, Capua was captured by the Samnites'; after the Etruscans abandoned Campania 'in the 5th century BC', the Samnites 'conquered the region, including Pompeii and Herculaneum', 'conquered Cumae, but failed to take Naples' (Samnites page). Caserta province is Capua's from 424 (capua dossier, -424..-343): the Samnites' share is Campania without Caserta.

union.text: the Campanian plain of Capua, Pompeii and Herculaneum, Cumae

ledger.note: 343-341 BC: the First Samnite War. 'In 343 BC', Capua 'sought Roman help against its conquerors' (Capua page); Livy 'says the war began in 343 BC after the Campanians allied with Rome'; peace after 'three Samnite defeats and a Roman invasion' (infobox 343-341). The Liris had been the treaty line since 354 ('In 354 BC, they agreed to set their border at the Liris River').

union.text: the Campanian plain of Capua, Pompeii and Herculaneum, Cumae

ledger.note: 341 BC: peace; Rome 'withdrew after the Latin revolt' (expansion page).

region.text: the Campanian plain of Capua, Pompeii and Herculaneum, Cumae

ledger.note: 338 BC: Campania to Rome. Capua's 'submission to Rome' is dated 338 and 'The citizens of Capua received the civitas sine suffragio'; the Campanians of the plain had allied with Rome in 343 and fought the Latin War with the Latins (Vesuvius 340). Drawn as the loss of the Campanian plain; the hill country toward Nola stays Samnite until 304. The loss covers the Samnite Campania, that is Campania without Caserta (Capua's own land, which went to Rome in 343, capua /ledger/1).
328 BC: 'Fregellae (328 BC): A Roman colony was founded there; the Samnites later took it' (and lost it again).

notes: New state, not in Cliopatria (the brief's 'Italic peoples'). Samnium is drawn as the four modern provinces of the Samnite heartland; Campania is Samnite 424-338 (Capua captured c. 424; Capua's 'submission to Rome' 338 with civitas sine suffragio). The state ends in 290 with the Third Samnite War ('subjugated in 290 BC'); the roman-republic dossier tints Samnium as allied land 290-91 and the Social War confederation (italian-city-states) carries the Samnite rising of 91-87. The wikidata id Q207400 is from memory and unverified (wikidata.org unreachable). Gazetteer: 'Samnium', 'Bovianum', 'Venusia', 'Fregellae', 'Luceria' absent (admin1 unions and circles used). Revised 2026-10-19 after review: keyframes added; the Campania gained in 424 and lost in 338 is now Campania without Caserta (Capua's land 424-343, capua dossier); the dossier follows roman-republic's vassal model (vassal_start 290, vassal_end 91) and ends in 91 with a dissolve to italian-city-states instead of 290; that dossier names roman-republic as its only predecessor, so the hand-over is one-sided; the Samnites' resistance to Sulla (Colline Gate, 82, Samnites page) is not drawn after the confederation ends in 88. The Samnites page does not mention Capua or 424; the 424 gain cites the Capua page. Wikidata Q207400 was from memory (unverified) and is set to null.
